ATTACK CHAINS & ESCALATION PATHS

Public Redis RCE to Cloud Metadata SSRF Compromise

An unauthenticated attacker connects to the exposed Redis port, injects a rogue webhook configuration payload, and pivots through the SSRF endpoint to query the AWS IMDSv1 instance metadata service to steal node credentials.

1

Attacker connects to Redis instance exposed on port 6379 without authentication

2

Attacker extracts internal API tokens and webhook configurations from db0 cache keys

3

Attacker invokes the /api/webhooks/test endpoint passing AWS Instance Metadata Service IP (169.254.169.254)

4

Attacker exfiltrates IAM Role temporary session credentials from IMDSv1

Impact

Full node takeover and unauthorized lateral movement into the ACME AWS Production environment allowing access to all customer databases.

REMEDIATION PRIORITY MATRIX
Priority Finding Category Remediation Action
CRITICAL Unauthenticated Redis Instance Exposed to Public Subnet NETWORK Restrict port 6379 to VPC-internal access only via Security Group rules and enable requirepass authentication.
HIGH Broken Object Level Authorization (BOLA) in User Profile Export API Implement object-level ownership checks verifying that the authenticated user ID matches the requested resource ID before returning profile records.
HIGH Hardcoded AWS Production IAM Access Key in Static Bundle AUTH Revoke the exposed access key AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE immediately in AWS IAM, audit CloudTrail logs, and migrate to IAM Roles for EC2/EKS.
MEDIUM Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) via Webhook Verification WEB Enforce strict allowlists of authorized target domains, disable following HTTP redirects, and block local/private IP ranges (127.0.0.0/8, 169.254.169.254, 10.0.0.0/8).
LOW Missing Strict-Transport-Security (HSTS) Header on Port 8443 SSL Add Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains; preload header to all TLS-enabled responses.
